memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as male servants do. If she does not please the master who has selected her for himself, he must let her be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, because he has broken faith with her." - Exodus 21:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses reflect a world very different from ours, where a poor family might place a daughter into a household, often as a wife. To our ears the arrangement sounds troubling. But look closely and you will see God protecting the most vulnerable person in the situation. This young woman could not simply be used and discarded. If faith was broken with her, she had rights — redemption, protection, provision. God refused to let her be treated as mere property.

We must be honest: these laws met a fallen culture where it was, not where God's ideal stood. Yet even here God is guarding the weak, restraining exploitation, insisting that a vulnerable girl carries dignity that must be honoured. That heartbeat runs straight through Scripture to Jesus, who lifted up women, children, and outsiders whom society overlooked.

God still sees the ones others use and forget. If you feel small, unseen, or taken advantage of, know that the God of the Bible has always defended people like you. And He calls us to do the same — to protect, never to exploit.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Who around me is vulnerable and in need of protection rather than use?
Do I believe God sees my own worth even when others overlook me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You defend the weak and see the forgotten. Give me eyes for the vulnerable and a heart that protects rather than exploits. Amen.
